chunks: Certainly, we and you were on amiable terms as you say but difference arose between us and you the other day, when we accepted belief (īmān) and you rejected it. Today the position is that we are steadfast (in the belief) but you are creating mischief. Those of you who accepted Islam did so reluctantly and that too when all the chief men had accepted Islam and joined the Messenger of Allāh (may Allāh bless him and his descendants).

key_terms.أَنْفُ: The chief men or nobles (literally 'the nose')

ai.seo_question: What is the contrast between the Shia and the general public in Nahj al-Balagha's response to Muawiya?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) articulates the theological schism between the Ahl al-Bayy and the Umayyad faction, attributing the division to the shift from voluntary unity to forced conformity under Muawiya’s rule. This passage underscores the Shia concept of *fitna* (trial/distinction), where steadfastness in faith contrasts with the superficial, coerced Islam of the masses who lacked the spiritual depth of the Prophet's inner circle.
